subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer presented a painted rock to Prefect Terjon as evidence, was shocked by the rejection, and later bowed out to return to the temple for prayers.
source_quote: Calmer asked, "Tomorrow at the same time?"

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr retrieved the painted rock from Prefect Terjon after questioning its worth, carried it to Burne and Rufus, and recognized the connection between the rock and the missing blueprints.
source_quote: Zephyr said, "If this rock is so worthless, why keep it?"

subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia recognized the town’s lack of secrets, truthfully disclosed their interactions to Jaroo, and led the group to Elder Kenter’s compound to secure local political support.
source_quote: Zinia muttered, "We should go talk to the village elder."

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia observed the two sons of Elder Kenter carefully grooming horses and inferred their pride in possessions.
source_quote: Sequoia thought that they must be very proud of their possessions.

subject: Prefect Terjon
fact: Prefect Terjon dismissed the rock as a painted trinket, refused to keep it initially, then changed his mind and retained it, later tossing it to Zephyr after being provoked.
source_quote: Terjon muttered, "You’re right. It is worthless."

subject: Burne
fact: Burne and Rufus connected the painted rock to the missing blueprints, recognized sabotage, and commissioned the party to investigate the encampment workers.
source_quote: Burne muttered, "This is it?"

subject: Rufus
fact: Rufus discovered charcoal dust on returned blueprints, suspected a saboteur working with bandits, and concluded the thief was among the encampment workers.
source_quote: Rufus whispered, "We may have a job for you."

subject: Ostler
fact: Ostler, the innkeeper, enforced a three-night minimum stay policy and noted that adventurers had not spoken to the Druid, hinting at unresolved tension.
source_quote: Ostler said, "I’ll believe it when he says so."

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo, the Druid, demanded deeper evidence from the moathouse, blessed the party with Beory’s favor and a healing potion after learning they had spoken to Terjon, Burne, and Rufus.
source_quote: Jaroo shouted, "Who else have you spoken to?"

subject: Elder Kenter
fact: Elder Kenter welcomed the party to his compound, acknowledged Beory’s blessings, and presided over a household of five families and servants, representing the town’s political core.
source_quote: Kenter toasted, "The Blessings of Beory."

subject: Kenter's Household
fact: The household of Elder Kenter consists of five families: the elder and his wife, four sons and their wives, with children and servants, forming a defensible and influential local power structure.
source_quote: Zinia discovered that the compound has five families: the village elder and his wife, the four sons and their wives. A gaggle of children... servants here as well.

subject: Local Militia
fact: The local militia has orders to bring the party to Burne and Rufus at the Inn of the Welcome Wench, indicating structured coordination between town authority and enforcement.
source_quote: They are local militia members and have orders to bring the four to Burne and Refus, who are currently drinking at the Inn of the Welcome Wench.

subject: painted rock
fact: The painted rock, found on a bandit’s body, was dismissed as worthless by Terjon, accepted by Zephyr, and later recognized by Burne and Rufus as a clue linked to charcoal dust on stolen blueprints.
source_quote: Terjon said, "You bring me a painted rock."

subject: blueprints for the keep
fact: The blueprints for the keep were reported missing, later returned with traces of charcoal dust, suggesting an internal copy operation by a saboteur among the encampment workers.
source_quote: Rufus said, "I found them missing... traces of charcoal dust on them."

subject: blueprint theft investigation commissioned
fact: Burne and Rufus, convinced by the rock’s connection to the charcoal-dusted blueprints, formally commissioned the party to investigate the encampment workers for sabotage.
source_quote: Rufus said, "You must go and find the thief."

subject: Druid’s blessing granted
fact: After learning the party had spoken to Terjon, Burne, and Rufus, Jaroo granted them Beory’s blessing and a healing potion, signaling his approval and hidden knowledge of their actions.
source_quote: Jaroo offered them the blessing of Beory and a healing potion.

subject: three-night inn stay enforced
fact: Ostler enforced a policy that adventurers must stay at the Inn for a minimum of three nights, and any goods left behind are sold after three days.
source_quote: Ostler said, "adventurers have a minimum three-night stay at the Inn. And as a matter of policy, any goods left behind are sold after three days."

subject: identity of the saboteur
fact: The saboteur is suspected to be a worker in the encampment who collaborated with the bandits, but their identity remains unknown and must be uncovered.
source_quote: Rufus said, "I am convinced it is one of the workers in the encampments."

subject: Druid’s hidden agenda
fact: The Druid’s apparent approval and delayed blessing suggest he knew of the party’s prior dealings and is waiting for them to engage him directly before revealing deeper truths.
source_quote: Ostler said, "I’ll believe it when he says so, which will happen after you talk to him about whatever you talked to Burne, Rufus, and Terjon about."

subject: Elder Kenter’s Compound
fact: Elder Kenter’s compound is a defensible residence with an eight-foot-high stone wall and heavy gate, housing five families, children, and servants, serving as the political heart of the village.
source_quote: It is the residence of some well-to-do folk and easily defensible in times of trouble.

subject: Inn of the Welcome Wench
fact: The Inn of the Welcome Wench is where Burne and Rufus are drinking and where the party receives their mission; it is a hub of local intelligence and social interaction.
source_quote: Burne and Refus are sitting at the table, drinking.

subject: Temple of St. Cuthbert
fact: The Temple of St. Cuthbert is where Prefect Terjon resides and where the painted rock was first evaluated; it is a center of civic authority and religious influence.
source_quote: Once inside the temple of St. Cuthbert, Calmer excitedly explains to Prefect Terjon...

subject: Moathouse
fact: The Moathouse is the site of prior investigations and remains the target for deeper evidence, as repeatedly demanded by town leaders including Jaroo and Ostler.
source_quote: Ostler admonished, "You must go deeper into the moathouse and find more evidence."

subject: bandits
fact: Bandits were defeated and one confessed, yielding the painted rock; they are suspected of colluding with a saboteur among the encampment workers.
source_quote: The stone's strange markings suggest elemental evil, and after a confession from one of the bandits...

subject: Planting 16, 579
fact: The events of the chapter occur on Planting 16, 579, marking the timeline of the recruitment, loaded dice, and midnight whispers.
source_quote: Date: Planting 16, 579
